title: Ashari vs Maturidi vs Athari
description: Test your theological orientation and discover which Sunni creed school your beliefs align with most.

questions.text: How do you understand Allah's attributes such as Hand, Face, and Eye?

options.text: Affirm them as real but not like creation, avoiding any interpretation
Affirm them and interpret metaphorically if reason and language require
Affirm them but prefer rational harmony through linguistic ta'wil

questions.text: What is the role of reason ('aql) in understanding belief (aqidah)?

options.text: A supporting tool, but revelation is primary
A decisive tool for establishing belief before revelation
Limited role, it cannot judge divine matters

questions.text: How should apparent contradictions between reason and revelation be resolved?

options.text: Revelation takes precedence and reason submits
Both must be reconciled through interpretation
Reason clarifies meaning within revelation's limits

questions.text: How do you define human action and divine decree (qadar)?

options.text: Humans acquire acts (kasb) created by Allah
Humans have real power granted by Allah, yet dependent
All actions are created and willed directly by Allah

questions.text: What is your stance on ta'wil (figurative interpretation)?

options.text: Permitted only with necessity and linguistic proof
Used more broadly to maintain rational coherence
Avoided; texts accepted without interpretation

questions.text: How do you interpret Allah's speech (kalam Allah)?

options.text: Uncreated in meaning but created in letters and sounds
Eternal both in meaning and type, expressed through created sounds
Uncreated and literal, without distinction of type or sound
Affirmation by tongue and heart; actions perfect but not define it
Affirmation by heart and tongue, actions reflect but not determine faith
Belief, word, and deed together define faith and can increase or decrease

questions.text: How should we classify a Muslim who commits a major sin?

options.text: Still a believer; judged by Allah's will
Still a believer with deficient faith
A believer but faith decreases; avoid takfir

questions.text: What is the proper use of kalam (theological reasoning)?

options.text: Necessary to defend belief and clarify ambiguities
Useful within reason's bounds and moral purpose
Avoided entirely; it leads to misguidance

questions.text: How do you view the relationship between revelation and science or philosophy?

options.text: Compatible if revelation remains superior
Mutually supportive when reason stays moral
Philosophy is secondary; revelation is the ultimate guide

Ashari.name: Ashari
Ashari.description: Your theological orientation aligns most closely with the Ashari school. Asharis emphasize the use of reason to defend and clarify Islamic beliefs, while maintaining that revelation is primary. They use ta'wil (interpretation) when necessary and believe in the concept of kasb (acquisition) regarding human actions.

Maturidi.name: Maturidi
Maturidi.description: Your theological orientation aligns most closely with the Maturidi school. Maturidis give reason a more decisive role in establishing belief and use ta'wil more broadly to maintain rational coherence. They believe humans have real power granted by Allah and emphasize the harmony between reason and revelation.

Athari.name: Athari
Athari.description: Your theological orientation aligns most closely with the Athari school. Atharis emphasize accepting texts without interpretation (ta'wil), affirming Allah's attributes as they are mentioned without metaphorical interpretation. They believe revelation takes precedence over reason in matters of faith and that faith includes belief, word, and deed.
